Class EndlessMode

java.lang.Object
backend.logic.EndlessMode
public class EndlessMode extends Object
EndlessMode.java

Encapsulates all backend logic for the Endless game mode (FR 3.1.14 - extra functional requirement). Endless mode reuses the regular gameplay screen with the following modified rules (Design Doc Section 4.2.5):

  • Survival scoring. The player earns points for every successful attack or defend phase. Points scale with the current stage so later phases are worth more, rewarding endurance.
  • Progressive difficulty. Every 5 phases the stage advances, which moves the active Difficulty tier upward (EASY -> MEDIUM -> HARD) and then increases an intra-HARD speed multiplier. getCurrentDifficulty() returns the tier the WordBank should use for word selection on the current phase.
  • Run ends when the player runs out of lives or chooses to exit. endSession() marks the session inactive.

Turn structure

The game loop calls onPhaseCompleted(int, long, int) after each successful attack or defend phase (matching the tutorial's description that "every time you successfully attack or defend, you receive score"). The result is the points awarded for that phase.

No GUI imports

This class has no GUI imports. All state is queried by the game loop / controller and passed to the GUI layer.

Design Documentation Section 3.2.10, 4.2.5; FR 3.1.1 Section 4 (difficulty scaling), FR 3.1.14 (extra feature - endless mode).

Team 49 - CS2212B Winter 2026

    • onPhaseCompleted

      public int onPhaseCompleted(int wordPointValue, long elapsedMs, int errorsMade)
      Records that the player successfully completed a phase (attack or defend) and updates all internal counters. Call this once per successful phase, regardless of whether it was an attack or a defend.

      The returned points value should be added to the player's displayed score by the game loop. It is also accumulated in getTotalScore() for use when building the SessionResult at run end.

      Parameters:
      wordPointValue - the pointValue of the word that was just typed, as loaded from words.csv (Section 5.3)
      elapsedMs - milliseconds taken to type the word
      errorsMade - number of incorrect keystrokes during this phase
      Returns:
      the points awarded for this phase (always Ã¢â€°Â¥ 0)

    • getAttackDamage

      public int getAttackDamage()
      Returns the amount of damage a successful attack phase deals to the opponent.

      The frontend/controller may still replenish the opponent between waves to preserve the endless loop, but successful attacks in Endless mode should use the normal base damage and then apply any power-up multipliers.

      Returns:

    • getCurrentDifficulty

      public Difficulty getCurrentDifficulty()
      Returns the Difficulty tier that should be passed to WordBank.getRandomWord(String) (or equivalent) when selecting the next word. The tier advances as the stage increases:
      • Stages 1-3-1 -> Difficulty.EASY
      • Stages 3-6-1 -> Difficulty.MEDIUM
      • Stages 6+ -> Difficulty.HARD
      Returns:
      the active difficulty tier for this stage

    • calculatePhaseScore

      public int calculatePhaseScore(int wordPointValue, long elapsedMs, int errorsMade)
      Calculates the score awarded for a single successfully completed phase.

      Formula (matches the design doc's description that score is based on word difficulty and how fast it was typed, Section 4.2.2 Tutorial screen):

        stageMultiplier = currentStage
  base            = wordPointValue * stageMultiplier
  errorPenalty    = errorsMade * 10
  total           = max(0, base - errorPenalty)

      A speed bonus is deliberately not included here because the timer mechanics in the turn-based attack/defend structure are handled by the gameplay timer, and the design doc places the time-based scoring formula in ScoreCalculator, not in the mode-specific class.

      Parameters:
      wordPointValue - the CSV pointValue of the completed word
      elapsedMs - milliseconds taken (retained for future use / forwarding to ScoreCalculator)
      errorsMade - incorrect keystrokes during this phase
      Returns:
      points to award (always Ã¢â€°Â¥ 0)

    • endSession

      public void endSession()
      Marks the session as inactive. Call this when the player's HP reaches 0 or they choose to exit (Design Doc Section 4.2.5 - "run ends when your health reaches 0, or when you choose to exit").

      After calling this, the game loop should call GameSession.buildResult() to package the final SessionResult for PlayerStats.updateAfterSession().

    • reset

      public void reset()
      Resets all counters to their starting values, ready for a new run. Called by the constructor and may be called again to restart endless mode without constructing a new instance.
